title: Category Specialists: Filling a Need
markdown:
<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** A category specialist can fix a category you are close in. He cannot fix one you have already lost. Punt rankings make one-category players look like top 100 picks, but our league counts all 9 categories every week. So treat specialists as late or in-season fillers, and check your category standings before every late bid or FAB claim.

## Punt rankings flatter specialists

Many rankings remove a player's weak categories before they rank him. Measured that way, a one-category specialist can look like a top 100 player. That does not make him a top 100 player in a standard league like ours. Every week we play all 9 categories, so his weak ones still count against you. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1527))

Big men who are elite only in blocks, FG% and rebounds get overdrafted in category leagues. Do not pay a third-round price for that profile. Remember that FG% and FT% are team ratios in our league. A big man with a bad FT% on real volume can drag your whole team's FT% down. ([07-02](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1083))

The same warning applies to guards and wings. High steals alone should not raise what you pay for a player. A shooting guard who only makes threes, with no rebounds or assists, is a bad fantasy profile unless he is elite at threes. ([09-09](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2462), [07-05](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=3864))

## Fill a need, not a lost cause

Track your category strengths and weaknesses during the auction itself. Then bid to fill a need, for example a big man for rebounds or a guard for assists. After each player you win, note where you stand in PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK and 3PTM. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=925))

Do not buy a one-category specialist to rescue a category that is already too weak to recover. Say you have filled most of your 12 spots and sit far behind in a category. One cheap specialist will not win it for you in a weekly matchup. Spend those late dollars on a category where one player can swing the result. ([09-15](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166))

Buying a specialist early has its own cost. A player who helps in only two categories leaves holes elsewhere, and you then have to fill them with your remaining budget. In a 200 USD auction, save the clear one-category buys for the late stage, after your core is set. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=960))

## When to reach: the experts disagree

The experts disagree on reaching. One side says you sometimes have to pay a bit early to fill a need, such as assists, and that a reach is fine if it fits your build, so you need not be rigid about value. The other side says that when you are weak in a category like assists, you should not chase it too hard. For our league, the middle path is this: reach a few dollars for a need that fits your planned build, and stop if you are bidding only to patch a weakness. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1391), [09-19](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=616), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=864))

## How to use specialists in our league

Before the 2026-10-18 auction, choose the build you want and the categories you plan to give up. During the auction, check that build after each win. Once your first 9 or 10 players are set, use the final roster spots on specialists for categories you are close in. Do not use them on a category you already plan to punt. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=925), [09-15](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166))

Only 144 players are drafted, so many specialists will go undrafted and sit on waivers. Pay 1 USD for a specialist ranked near the edge of the pool only when he fills a real need for your build. Otherwise let him go and claim him later. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1527), [09-15](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166))

The same rule applies in season. Waivers process daily, and you get at most 6 acquisitions per week. Spend FAB and adds on a specialist when a category is close against this week's opponent. Do not spend them on a category that is already gone. If a category stays weak all season, trade for a better all-around player before the 2027-03-04 deadline instead of collecting specialists for our playoff weeks 19 to 21. ([09-15](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=864), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=960))

## Players

Prices in USD. Yahoo and ESPN: rank and average auction cost for 2026-27.

### Mid-auction category buys

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Tyrese Haliburton](#player/215) | IND | G | 10 | 45.4 | 12 | 39.1 | not drafted | Elite assists plus useful threes, steals and FT%, but managed minutes and rested back-to-backs keep experts below his Yahoo rank. |
| [Karl-Anthony Towns](#player/560) | NYK | F,C | 16 | 40.0 | 19 | 34.5 | 46 | Big rebound numbers and a FT% that helps for a big, with turnovers as his only weak category, though experts warn he is going too high. |
| [Trae Young](#player/617) | WAS | G | 18 | 33.6 | 47 | 33.4 | 44 | A top-five passer with elite FT% who costs you FG% and turnovers, so he fits punt FG% or punt TO builds. |
| [Kawhi Leonard](#player/331) | TOR | G,F | 37 | 32.6 | 18 | 26.0 | 20 | Standout steals with strong points and FT% per game, but knee and load management cut his games, and three Toronto back-to-backs fall in our playoffs. |
| [Josh Giddey](#player/190) | CHI | G | 19 | 35.0 | 36 | 34.0 | 31 | Elite assists and strong rebounds that work best on punt TO, with his FT% and his usage next to Powell and Buzelis as early checks. |
| [LaMelo Ball](#player/27) | MIN | G | 24 | 30.2 | 22 | 27.2 | 29 | A threes and assists source for punt FG% and punt TO builds, with ankle risk and a two-game playoff week as reasons to stay at the low end. |
| [Devin Booker](#player/51) | PHX | G | 23 | 28.4 | 40 | 32.7 | 45 | A points source with elite FT% whose value depends on whether he still runs the offense next to Jalen Green. |
| [Stephen Curry](#player/124) | GSW | G | 25 | 30.6 | 33 | 24.5 | 42 | Elite threes and points per game, but his knee, his age and 43 games played last season mean you should not pay a premium. |
| [Jalen Brunson](#player/72) | NYK | G | 29 | 32.6 | 30 | 42.9 | 31 | Points on high usage plus threes, FT% and assists, but the Knicks' careful minutes plan and his wrist surgery make him a round 4 player for experts. |
| [James Harden](#player/219) | CLE | G | 31 | 19.4 | 25 | 28.0 | 42 | An elite assist source for punt FG% and punt TO builds, and experts say not round two, so last season's price would be an overpay. |
| [Domantas Sabonis](#player/491) | SAC | F,C | 35 | 22.6 | 32 | 39.3 | 41 | About 13.7 projected rebounds plus FG% and assists from the C spot, a punt TO fit that experts place in rounds 3 to 4. |
| [Anthony Davis](#player/129) | WAS | F,C | 45 | 21.8 | 14 | 24.6 | 54 | Elite blocks and rebounds with no weak category, but projected 58 to 61 games keep him a round 3 buy. |
| [Evan Mobley](#player/392) | CLE | F,C | 27 | 23.6 | 27 | 19.9 | 36 | Blocks, rebounds and FG% count fully in punt FT% builds, and he finished 41st in categories last season, so do not repeat last year's price. |
| [Jalen Duren](#player/154) | DET | C | 33 | 18.2 | 23 | 24.1 | 14 | A FG% and rebounds anchor who makes no threes, a punt 3PM fit whom experts see in rounds 3 to 4. |
| [Brandon Miller](#player/381) | CHA | F | 39 | 19.2 | 54 | 7.3 | 20 | Threes, points and FT% for punt FG% and punt TO builds, and a third-round player if his shoulder checks out before the auction. |

### Value at price

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Dyson Daniels](#player/128) | ATL | G,F | 61 | 4.4 | 38 | 9.7 | 28 | Projected 2.2 steals plus assists, rebounds and FG%, so he gives punt FT% and punt 3PM builds more than steals alone. |
| [Ausar Thompson](#player/549) | DET | G,F | 77 | 3.2 | 78 | 2.4 | 16 | Elite steals with good FG%, rebounds and blocks, and experts say he should go clearly above his site ranks. |
| [Darius Garland](#player/185) | LAC | G | 54 | 6.6 | 53 | 12.8 | 11 | Assists, threes and FT% from a likely top 50 guard who goes cheap on Yahoo, with his toe health as the main check. |
| [Jaren Jackson Jr.](#player/265) | UTA | F,C | 42 | 13.4 | 71 | 5.0 | 29 | A blocks source that experts rank near 36th, well above his market cost, who can carry blocks next to low-assist bigs. |
| [Matas Buzelis](#player/80) | CHI | F | 69 | 9.0 | 59 | 4.2 | 12 | Real blocks with no weak category, and experts agree he is a top 50 breakout pick. |
| [Kon Knueppel](#player/315) | CHA | G,F | 64 | 15.8 | 39 | 15.0 | not drafted | About 3.7 projected threes with solid FT%, but weak steals and blocks mean he only fits builds that can carry those. |
| [Walker Kessler](#player/310) | LAL | C | 41 | 18.8 | 45 | 8.4 | 15 | A three-category center (BLK, REB, FG%) with a bad FT%, the type that gets overdrafted, so keep him near his ESPN level and on punt FT builds. |
| [Donovan Clingan](#player/108) | POR | C | 38 | 12.0 | 43 | 6.0 | 7 | Rebounds and blocks with a weak FT% and little else, so he is a big-man specialist only at a low price. |
| [Rudy Gobert](#player/196) | MIN | C | 82 | 7.2 | 55 | 4.7 | 10 | A punt FT% center with rebounds, blocks and about 67% FG, but his FT% is a big drag in any other build. |
| [Ivica Zubac](#player/620) | IND | C | 57 | 8.2 | 81 | 3.5 | 20 | A FG% and rebounds anchor for punt 3PM and punt STL builds, fair at his Yahoo average cost, not his Yahoo value. |
| [Alex Sarr](#player/496) | WAS | C | 63 | 7.0 | 61 | 3.3 | 9 | About 1.9 projected blocks even if Davis takes his spot at the rim, so he is worth buying as a blocks specialist, not at the price his rank suggests. |
| [Zach Edey](#player/158) | MEM | C | 70 | 7.2 | 113 | 1.4 | 2 | FG%, rebounds and blocks for big-man builds that punt TO, if you accept the ankle risk. |
| [Joel Embiid](#player/165) | PHI | C | 53 | 7.4 | 88 | 8.3 | 24 | Elite per-game points and FT% from a center, but 49 to 54 projected games make him a mid-round buy only. |

### Avoid at price

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Chet Holmgren](#player/243) | OKC | F,C | 28 | 30.6 | 51 | 10.1 | 32 | Elite blocks with no weak category, but experts say Yahoo's round-two price is too high, so target him only well below it. |
| [Stephon Castle](#player/93) | SAS | G | 76 | 6.6 | 92 | 10.4 | 1 | About 7.3 projected assists for punt FT% and punt TO builds, but experts fade him at his Yahoo ADP. |

### Late flyers

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Myles Turner](#player/564) | MIL | C | 101 | 1.0 | 93 | 1.0 | 20 | Blocks and threes from a center for punt FG% builds, fine late but not worth a top-100 price. |
| [Jalen Suggs](#player/539) | ORL | G | 94 | 2.8 | 142 | 0.4 | 1 | Steals for builds that can absorb his weak FG% and turnovers, with about 20 missed games to plan for. |
| [Kevin Porter Jr.](#player/450) | MIL | G | 158 | 1.0 | 107 | 1.1 | 3 | Steals and assists for punt 3PM builds, and easy to drop if he does not start or reach 27 minutes. |
| [Cason Wallace](#player/582) | OKC | G,F | 128 | 1.0 | 109 | 0.5 | 1 | Steals with low turnovers but little scoring, rebounding or passing, so he only suits builds chasing steals. |
| [Khaman Maluach](#player/344) | PHX | C | 118 | 1.5 | 202 | 0.1 | not drafted | Blocks plus some rebounds and FG% near our 144-player cutoff, for punt AST and punt STL builds, if he starts while Mark Williams is out. |
| [Yves Missi](#player/387) | NOP | C | 143 | - | 164 | 0.0 | 2 | Blocks with FG% on low volume and few turnovers, and back to waivers if he does not start over Derik Queen. |
| [Scotty Pippen Jr.](#player/444) | MEM | G | 183 | - | 144 | 0.2 | not drafted | His value is almost all steals and his projected 2.5 turnovers hurt, so he is a last pick or a waiver option only. |
| [Isaiah Stewart](#player/535) | MEM | F,C | 174 | 0.0 | 146 | 0.1 | not drafted | Blocks plus FG% on low volume, worth a pick or an early claim only if Edey stays out. |

### Waiver watch

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Dereck Lively II](#player/335) | DAL | C | 166 | - | 143 | 0.1 | 3 | A broken foot keeps him out until around Thanksgiving, so watch waivers for his blocks and FG% if he later wins the starting job. |
| [Robert Williams III](#player/611) | POR | C | 202 | - | 165 | 0.0 | not drafted | Blocks and FG% in under 20 minutes, a waiver add if his minutes climb or Clingan misses time, though back-to-back rest hurts in weeks 19 to 21. |
| [De'Anthony Melton](#player/376) | GSW | G | 245 | - | 180 | 0.0 | not drafted | Steals with a low FG%, outside our draft pool, so add him only if he starts and plays about 28 minutes. |
| [Matisse Thybulle](#player/552) | LAL | G,F | 343 | - | 219 | 0.0 | not drafted | A pure steals specialist in under 20 minutes, worth a waiver pickup only if his minutes rise above 16 and he stays healthy. |

- Giannis Antetokounmpo: Build anchor priced near 60 USD, not a category filler.

- Jayson Tatum: Top-8 multi-category forward priced near 55 USD.
